reviews.review:
I give the game an 8/10 

If you'd like reasons, continue reading.

	First, I'd like to say, I am happy with what the games looks to achieve. You're an Immune Survivor that takes the Roll of a Cleaner (A mercenary/specialist that deals with Anti-Infected missions and tasks) which pits against some of the most interesting enemies. Because you are immune, you are sent on almost all these missions. You can pick up on the lore listening to the banter and dialogue of the game. 
	Now what is great about the game?
	The customization is something that brings the rating high. The current perk deck I run is a Sniper Based setup. I'm sure a few folks when reading that are like: "sNiPeRs?!? WHY!?" Well, the perk setup allows me to have 100% Accuracy, which brings the cross hairs to the size of a pinhead and with 100% reload speed. I take 25% less damage as well and my sidearm has unlimited ammo. I specialize mainly in taking down the Special variants of Infected that normally anyone would have to dump bullets into. That’s just one of MANY builds you can come up with, with the current perk system. (More Cards are coming as well)
	Coupled with each “Cleaner” are perks associated with themselves that can synergize well with a build of the players choice, the possibilities are great!
	With that being said, I have completed the game a few times. I noticed in the other reviews that there are difficulty complains…
I’ll mention the difficulty complains here because I find the difficulty refreshing.
	During the beta, a large sum of players complained that the game was too easy… It needed to be adjusted. Some of those players are now saying the game is too hard. I, personally think the game difficulty is good, it needs to be challenging and be able to challenge the multitudes of “Headass Nonsense” I can come with using the Perk Deck system. The developers purposely made the game more difficult, which eventually you will find won’t mean anything when you are dropping the Ogre with 1 shot to almost 40% life or beating down the berserker with a fire-axe an under 6 seconds (Which Is the standing record in my group).
	My advice would be to play recruit (Which is honestly Normal difficulty) until you have enough supply points (Currency to buy perk cards) to really get a base foundation for the type of build you want to run. THIS IS NOT LEFT 4 DEAD, STOP COMPARING IT TO THAT GAME SERIES. 
	
	What is wrong with the game?
	There are bugs, several bugs, one of which is, if you join a pre-existing campaign in a later chapter of an ACT you can unlock your entire perk deck. I can’t beat the game like that, I don’t feel that is necessary and I’d like to do It legitimately. 
	There is no single player progression. I understand this one, because not all the time my group wants to play B4B and other player just want to zone out earning supply points smacking Ridden around, so the fact that this game didn’t have this in the beginning made me annoyed. 
	There should be a better tutorial for players. I’m not saying hold their hand, but honestly, I don’t think many folks know that the REEKER has its weak spot on the back of its neck… don’t believe me? Next time you log in, existing owners, check out the back of its neck… If the weak spot was its head, I’d be more comfortable.
	THE GRIND. Why is it, that modern games require so much grinding? This is where I understand folks who are turned off from the game. The fact I had to spend 5500 Supply Points to get a deck going to play the game, you must play the campaign SEVERAL Times over to get that many… I’m talking A LOT, or You reply to a mission which gives you an ample sum for minimal effort, but that shouldn’t be a method to gain supply points. It be given generously and when you gain all the perk points, be able to use the supply points for cosmetics, NOT DURING. I shouldn’t have to buy 7-8 cosmetics to get a perk that could potentially make the game 10x better… that’s honestly dumb. 
	The Price. Is it Worth $60 USD? Depends, I’ve had a lot of fun with it, but I see why some people believe it should be $40. I agree on the extent that, there isn’t much else to do other than smash the campaign over and over, but the PVP? Really nonexistent, because you can’t bring your campaign perk deck into pvp… for good reason mind you.

	That’s how I feel about the game, I give it an 8/10, Why so High after those complaints? I’ve had so much fun, BULLEYEING Tall boys and Reekers from across the map HIP Firing like an animal. The builds are incredible, and they make replaying the same maps incredibly fun. Especially with Friends who make builds which compliment one another. 
	So, Give the game a shot, pick it up at $30/$40 on sale, honestly. I think it’s worth that.

As a player who recently joined the community, i have experienced any game breaking bugs, but some bugs which is to be expected. Issues such as ghsot recoils, cheesing some of the maps and connection issues and reconnection issues. With the new update coming, hopefully some of these bugs will be smoothed out and improved on. This is a left 4 dead 3 in a sense as it has the same mechanics, but with addition of cards and character specialise skills.
Update: Some patches and the christmas update has been rolled out, speedrunning a map is way harder than it used to be, but nightmare and veteran actually feels like the correct difficulty, issues with ghost recoil and reconnecting seemed to happen less. But there are still game breaking bugs which lessen the difficulty of nightmare significantly.

Okay, where to start.  Well, first, I'll get this out of the way: I really like this game and genuinely don't understand why it has a mixed rating.  My only guess is that perhaps people thought it was going to be exactly like L4D.  It has some similarities, but B4B plays more like World War Z.  I think that's a good thing, personally.  It forces you to work together and will punish you for trying to be a lone wolf.  Now, for a negative point, the game currently has no way to kick foolish people, ie via a vote.  They need to fix that.  Someone being a dough head can really make things frustrating at times.

So, the game plays more like World War Z than Left 4 Dead, as I mentioned.  Gun play is great.  There's a wide variety of weapons that each have their own characteristics, advantages and drawbacks to suit a wide range of preferences.  There's also a large number of sights, stocks, magazines and barrel attachments that will essentially give your weapon bonuses as you progress.  You can try all these out in the staging area to get a feel for what weapons and sights you like before getting into the game.

The zombie AI is decent.  The regular infected are basically just cannon fodder to get in your  way, although they alone CAN be overwhelming depending on what type of environment you're in.  They can also put a good hurt on you when you're trying to deal with the mutated ridden.  Point is, while they're easy to kill, they can still be dangerous.  Now for the mutated ridden, unlike L4D, you will get a steady stream of these buggers.  They can be easy to kill if you hit their weak spot, but some of them will protect that weak spot, in which case they can be a bullet sponge.  Some of the tougher ones you really have to flank to take down.  Teamwork.

Something B4B does differently is their card system.  So they have these decks that you build.  Each card will give you bonuses or abilities.  Every round you pick a card to play.  These cards may give you more ammo capacity, health from melee, more stamina, more efficient healing, different weapons etc.  Some cards even give a bonus to the entire team. 
 Each deck you build can be tailored to a different play style.  As you play the game, you get supply points that you use to buy new cards.  What makes things interesting is that the computer also gets to play its own cards which can alter the level and make things harder as you progress.  For example, sometimes the level will get covered in a thick fog. The ridden will gain resistance to damage except for headshots. The mutated can have armour covering their weak points.  More doors can be alarmed.  There's a wack of other things as well.  Keeps it interesting and challenging.

That really gets down to the core of what I like about this game.  It's challenging and it requires teamwork.  If I'm playing with random people then I search out the lowest difficulty level.  If I'm playing with friends then I'm okay trying it a tad harder.  Anyways, that's my take.  I like it.

Good game but ... now that I have played this game 1/2 off experience levels and all the cards, this will be honest review.  These are suggestions to fix, x) Players quit to frequent because games too long stretch and not enough continues to keep going x) Support Bots lack sense and stand in front of you looking back at you while you're firing during huge battle, mutants need AI help too.  x) servers are too variant one server will be so hard but then others will be easier ( I am not sure what drives that ); I don't mind hard but damn losing your continue at first two levels of the Act II makes people quit (then stuck with bots).  Things I like: co-op play, handicap cards perks, meh on clothes, adding bits to weapons to make better. In short, fix AI bots players, AI for mutants, breakup long maps verses short ones (episodes) or add extra continue.

Although it is not exactly like L4D it does follow as a spiritual successor pretty well, I was never a fan of the PVP in L4D so the lack of it didn't really bother me. I do like the card system adding randomness and tweaks to each run I just wish there were more variance in it as well as customization for the characters (hopefully some and new cleaners will be released a later date.) My only real gripe with the game and its not even in the developers hands is the player base there are either not enough people or some people play it on even the easiest difficulty way WAY to seriously by being a sweaty complaining, blaming, or insulting another player and leaving other then that I love playing it.
Super fun multiplayer!  A bit boring until dlc drops.
